bluf: MuteSix is a US paid media specialist, founded 2014, that calls itself the #1 most awarded Meta ad agency selling omnichannel media buying with in house creative to DTC brands, claiming $1.2B+ in direct client revenue and 27.1B+ impressions. The record reads as a company going quiet: its own Google ads stopped after 2026-05-18, no sitemap content changed after January 2026, and 17 of its 20 clients are names only. Horus reads it Neutral at 2. The one thing a rival should know: nothing on record describes what it does for any client, so every DTC name on its book is a question worth asking.
doing:
The positioning line reads: end to end performance marketing agency pairing data led omnichannel media buying with in house creative production to scale DTC and consumer brands. In plain words, a Meta buying shop that added channels and a studio. The headline claim is volume: $1.2B+ in direct client revenue driven and 27.1B+ impressions served, carried as claims.

The sold mix leads with Paid Social at score 3: it claims to be the most awarded Meta ad agency and runs separate TikTok, Snapchat and Pinterest pages and case studies, with Meta Business Partner the one listed partner. Four lines score 2 at core: Data & Measurement, where a Marketing Science team runs ETL, BigQuery and Tableau data products; Paid Search, with a Google Ads page and Apple Search and Google case studies on the homepage; Programmatic & CTV, with programmatic, TV/CTV, podcast, native and YouTube buying each on a service page; and Retail Media, with an Amazon Ads page and an Amazon ROAS case on the homepage. CRO, creator and email score 1; SEO, web, content, B2B, local and AI score 0; breadth 8. The proprietary item is Performance Studio, the in house creative production unit.

AI posture is null: the record holds no AI statement, service or content, and the AI Search and AI Automation lines score 0.

Dated moves: none, and no news items. The dated trail is case study pages: FUNBOY 2026-01-23, Hug Sleep 2026-01-22, Aera 2026-01-14, Brooklyn Candle Studio 2025-12-30, Dave 2025-11-28, then Twillory and Spoonful of Comfort in 2024 and Green Pan, Pinsy, Healthy Spot and Moon Juice in 2023. The deepening pass counted 170 case study URLs and a SmartRecruiters job widget with 0 jobs listed.

Pricing signals are absent. For a performance agency claiming $1.2B+ of client revenue, the record lists no offices, no employee count, no ownership, no AI line and no working case study page.
clients:
The client type on record is mixed, across DTC ecommerce, fashion and apparel, beauty and personal care, home goods and food and beverage; the home market is the US, with no city or office listed.

The record names 20 clients: 3 observed and 17 names only, all from case pages or slugs, none shared with another tracked agency. The 3 observed reads are an artefact: MeUndies, Sitka Salmon Shares and a row whose title is the WordPress error page are read as web build only because the fetched page carried the WordPress error title, not because any work is described. The case pages that did load returned script text rather than copy, so no excerpt says what any client came for. The names, with page dates where the record has them: FUNBOY (2026-01-23), Hug Sleep (2026-01-22), Aera (2026-01-14), Brooklyn Candle Studio (2025-12-30), Dave (2025-11-28), Twillory (2024-08-29), Spoonful of Comfort (2024-08-14), Green Pan (2023-03-24, also GreenPan), Pinsy (2023-03-24), Healthy Spot (2023-03-24), Moon Juice (2023-03-23), and from slugs alone Universal Standard, John Paul Mitchell Systems, Morphe, Gopuff and USA Today. Their needs are inferred from what the agency leads with, Meta paid social with paid search, programmatic and retail media behind it.

The observed mix is web build at share 1.0 on the 3 artefact rows. What this base needs next: DTC brands buying Meta and programmatic hours sit under KJ5 (The price of attention splits in two), and the record places MuteSix best for KJ9 (Measurement gets worse before it gets better) on its Marketing Science line; it is likely, with low confidence, that these clients ask next for measurement that survives signal loss, and a roughly even chance that the agency is still positioned to sell it, given the ad and content silence since May 2026.
house: Say and do: 2 of 3 tested lines are practised on its own house. Paid Search is corroborated: the Transparency Center shows 19 own Google ads, all text, advertiser Mutesix Inc., but 0 in the last 30 days and last shown 2026-05-18. Paid Social is corroborated on a pixel: linkedin_insight runs on its own site. LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: it sells paid social or B2B demand generation and the Ad Library shows 0 ads. The tag stack is full for a quiet site: GTM, Google Ads, LinkedIn Insight, HubSpot, Hotjar and RB2B on WordPress; no test tool was detected. Content velocity: the sitemap lists 727 URLs with 0 updated in 90 days and 1 in 365, and the own site read on 2026-09-29 found the newest pages dated 2026-01-23. The llms.txt test is null (not run), no AI crawlers are blocked and 0 AI topic URLs sit in the sitemap. No Meta or TikTok ad library reading is on record.
market:
Horus reads MuteSix at a tailwind index of 2, band Neutral, 24th percentile. It is best placed for KJ9, measurement getting worse before it gets better, driven by Data & Measurement at +2 (net 0.25). It is most exposed to KJ5, the price of attention splitting in two (net -0.241, Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV at -1 each). Best scenario fit is The Walled Oasis at 46/100. It is making P4; partial on P2 and P7; absent on P1, P6 and P8; P5 unknown; P3 not applicable.

Monsoon reads 39.8, band Doldrums, 8th percentile: migration 38.3 against displacement 41.3, both low. The verdict puts 38 of the index on the sold mix, Paid Search and Paid Social carrying the most movable hours, with automation overlapping 43% of them; the shore split is 65% South and Southeast Asia and 25% Latin America. No hub office is listed, so the footprint is inferred, and the record reads two onshore claims in its own words: the in house creative production of the positioning line and the Performance Studio unit.
openings:
The strongest opening is silence. MuteSix's own Google ads stopped after 2026-05-18, no sitemap content changed after January 2026, its case study pages return script text or a WordPress critical error, and 17 of its 20 clients are names only. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that the DTC brands on its book are contestable by a rival that asks who is running their Meta and Amazon spend now. The falsifier: a new Google ad, a dated 2026 case page that loads, or a SmartRecruiters job posting in the next compile.

The contradiction to lead with is LinkedIn: it sells paid social and runs 0 LinkedIn ads. The gap to lead with is proof: for an agency claiming $1.2B+ of client revenue, not one excerpt on record describes a result, so a rival whose cases load and carry numbers wins by default.

The offer that undercuts it is outcome priced media, since the record lists no pricing model (P5 unknown) and Horus places its one tailwind on Marketing Science; a rival that sells the measurement product it is best placed for takes the KJ9 ground. An offshore rate undercut is unlikely to matter at a displacement of 41.3.
watch: I4, Meta Q3 2026 average price per ad, next reading late October 2026: at or above +5% continues walled garden inflation and deepens the KJ5 exposure of its Meta led paid social and programmatic hours.

I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would raise the cost of its missing pricing model under KJ6.
Follow up the Transparency Center for any ad after 2026-05-18 and the SmartRecruiters job widget for any listing, either of which would reverse the going quiet read.
Follow up the case study pages (170 URLs counted) for a fetch that returns copy rather than script text or a WordPress error, which would move clients from names only to observed.
